summary: The study investigates the interfacial properties of Al2O3 films deposited on 4H-SiC(0001) using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The films were characterized using XPS and HRTEM, and the effects of annealing at 873 K and 1273 K on the interfacial oxide layer were analyzed. The presence of a thin SiOx layer was observed, which increased in thickness after annealing at 1273 K. The study also highlights the impact of annealing on the interfacial oxide thickness and the reduction of interface states.
evidence: Al2O3 was grown by ALD on Si-faced, n-type and p-type 4H-SiC samples using two different trimethylaluminum (TMA) precursors and O3 as an oxidant at a reactor temperature of 573 K.
